exposure: SARS-CoV-2 infection (acute vs nonacute, based on timing relative to delivery)
outcome: Placental pathology (fetal vascular malperfusion lesions, maternal vascular malperfusion lesions)
cohort: The study included universally tested SARS-CoV-2 positive pregnant women >20 weeks gestation, categorized by timing of infection relative to delivery, with a subset of SARS-CoV-2 negative women serving as controls.
finding: Acute SARS-CoV-2 infection (<14 days from delivery) was significantly associated with a higher frequency of fetal vascular malperfusion lesions compared to nonacute infection or SARS-CoV-2 negative controls, while maternal vascular malperfusion and obstetric/neonatal outcomes did not differ by timing of infection.
